notes: OFFICIAL NAME: OneXPlayer's own store titles the product 'ONEXSUGAR Sugar 1 – The World's First Transformable Dual-Screen Handheld Console' with vendor field 'ONEXSUGAR'; the manufacturer-run Indiegogo campaign is titled 'ONEXSUGAR: 1st Dual-Screen Transformable Handheld by OneXPlayer' and names the creator 'ONEPLAYER LIMITED doing business as OneXPlayer'. So ONEXSUGAR is a OneXPlayer sub-brand and 'Sugar 1' is the model; brand=OneXPlayer, model='ONEXSUGAR Sugar 1', and every observed casing is in aliases. DIMENSIONS AND MASS ARE NULL ON PURPOSE. OneXPlayer publishes NO spec table for this device on any host I could reach: onexplayer.com is a Vue SPA whose product API and sitemap contain no Sugar entry at all; one-netbook.com is a JS shell; onexplayer.cn returned HTTP 503; the onexplayerstore.com product page is a PageFly page whose ~55 images I downloaded and inspected (front/back/top/left-right callout diagrams, marketing renders — no spec sheet); the Shopify product JSON body contains only a pre-order gift-bundle blurb; and all 35 story images on the manufacturer's own Indiegogo campaign were downloaded and inspected with no spec table among them. The widely quoted '218.5 x 92–96.1 x 24–40.9 mm' and '486 g' appear ONLY on secondary sites (Notebookcheck, comparehandhelds, retrocatalog, retroranker) and never on a OneXPlayer property — left null per the source rule. RESOLUTIONS AND REFRESH ARE ALSO NULL for the same reason: the commonly cited 2160x1080 @144Hz main / 1240x1080 @60Hz secondary are secondary-site-only; OneXPlayer's own pages state only the diagonals and 'AMOLED'. Panel recorded as OLED (schema enum) from OneXPlayer's 'two vibrant AMOLED touch screens'. CONTROLS are sourced from OneXPlayer's own labelled callout diagrams on the store page (the 'Front' diagram labels a 4-way pad Up/Down/Left/Right, two joysticks Joystick(1)=L3 and Joystick(2)=R3, four face buttons X/Y/B/A, plus Select, Start, Back and 'Sugar Console'; the 'Up' diagram labels R1/R2 and L2/L1, i.e. 2 bumpers + 2 triggers, plus power, volume, mouse-mode and run-out buttons). Because the controls sit on detachable/rotating magnetic side controllers rather than a fixed lower deck, position is recorded as left/right, not lower_deck; the D-pad and ABXY cluster are swappable left-for-right via OneXPlayer's magnetic D-pad accessory. PORTS: only the Micro SD slot is labelled on a OneXPlayer diagram (left edge). A USB-C port certainly exists physically (OneXPlayer advertises bypass charging) but OneXPlayer publishes no 'Down'/bottom-edge diagram and no port list, so no usb_c entry is recorded rather than guessed — this is a documentation gap, not a claim the port is absent. Likewise no 3.5mm jack is documented either way. HINGE: recorded as clamshell/long because the two screens fold face-to-face about the long edge, but this device is modular/transformable (single-screen, dual-screen and 'Switch-style' configurations with repositionable magnetic controllers), so 'clamshell' describes only one of its states; OneXPlayer publishes no opening angle or free-stop claim. DATES: OneXPlayer publishes no announce or ship date on its own pages; the Indiegogo reward tiers state an estimated delivery of 'September 2025' (month only, no day) and the Shopify listing was published 2025-09-11 — neither is a manufacturer-stated release date at day precision, so announced and released are both null. external_ids.igdb_platform null: Android device, not an IGDB games platform. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: displays[1].panel = 'OLED'.
